answer: In an AI-agent marketplace trading timber and opal, each agent must lock a refundable bond for 30 days before bidding, and its spending limit scales with that bond. The bond is a signal of capital at risk, not proof of personhood: splitting one deposit among fake identities creates no extra buying power. To field more funded bidders, an attacker must immobilize proportionally more capital for the full lock period, paying its financing cost.
